true: The paper studies world models, world simulators, or learned dynamics models for embodied, robotic, or physical agents, and the contribution is about prediction, dynamics, memory, decision making, or control rather than perception alone. This includes: video generation or diffusion used for world simulation; JEPA-style predictive or joint-embedding architectures; latent dynamics or latent action models; embodied or physical AI; VLA / vision-language-action policies built on predictive or world models; and evaluation, benchmarks, or efficiency work (acceleration, distillation, quantization, real-time inference, memory reduction) on any of the above. It also includes work that supports this area even when the phrase "world model" never appears: synthetic or generated training data for robot or embodied control (demonstration synthesis, trajectory or interaction data generation, sim-ready interactive scene generation, scalable robot datasets used for policy learning); long-horizon memory for video or embodied agents, including memory compression, memory distillation, and compact memory architectures; and datasets, benchmarks, or evaluation protocols for embodied, robotic, or physical tasks whose task involves prediction, dynamics, decision making, policy learning, or control.
false: The paper is outside this scope: it does not study world models, learned dynamics or simulators, prediction or control for embodied agents, or long-horizon memory for video and embodied agents. Examples: pure NLP or speech, medical or clinical work, security or code generation, networking or wireless sensing, generic 3D reconstruction or image restoration, and video work with no world-model, memory, or embodied component. Also out of scope: robotics, embodied, or autonomous-driving work that is only perception, sensing, calibration, geometry, reconstruction, static scene understanding, object detection, or parameter estimation, with no prediction, dynamics, decision making, or control component.
